hints: Players move coins from higher stairs toward lower stairs; only the parity pattern in the relevant stair positions affects the outcome.
Treat the game as a sum of independent piles after using the equivalent Nim representation.
XOR the coin counts on every second stair, starting with the stair specified by the game rules.
analogy: Moves between stairs cancel paired positions, leaving only alternating stairs as Nim piles.
example: For counts 1,2,3, the alternating relevant pile(s) determine the XOR and hence the winner.
algorithm: For the standard Stair Game, XOR counts on even-indexed stairs (1-based stair 2,4,...) and declare first player winning iff nonzero.
correctness: A move changes one Nim component in the equivalent game; zero xor is losing and nonzero xor can be moved to zero.
